ev.q: PCs reported 2,405 e-cigarette and 16,248 cigarette exposure calls from across the United States
A greater proportion of e-cigarette exposure calls came from health-care facilities than cigarette exposure calls (12.8% versus 5.9%)
E-cigarette exposure calls per month increased from one in September 2010 to 215 in February 2014
Cigarette exposures were primarily among persons aged 0–5 years (94.9%)
e-cigarette exposure calls were more likely to report an adverse health effect after exposure than cigarette exposure calls (57.8% versus 36.0%)
CDC analyzed data on calls to U.S. poison centers
E-cigarette exposure calls per month increased from one in September 2010 to 215 in February 2014

methods_quotes.q: Statistical significance of differences (p<0.05) was assessed using chi-square tests.
E-cigarette exposure calls were compared with cigarette exposure calls by proportion of calls from health-care facilities
